chunks: Ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Dawud ibn Farqad who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:'
Verily the righteous deed goes to Paradise and paves the way for its doer, just as a man sends his servant boy to prepare a place for him.
As for those who believe and do good deeds, they prepare for themselves [their eternal abode].
ai.seo_question: How do good deeds prepare a person for Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates how righteous deeds precede the believer to Paradise, easing the journey much like a servant preparing lodging, thereby emphasizing the causal link between action and spiritual ease. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, highlights the Shia concept of *taysir* (facilitation) for the righteous, reinforcing that good works are not merely obligations but active preparations for the eternal abode. The Imam’s recitation of the verse underscores the mutual reinforcement of faith and action in securing one's place in the Hereafter.
